count.description: Occurrences within this section. Tag conceptual drawings, system architectures, anatomical/scientific schematics, or visual metaphors (including ASCII, SVG, or Mermaid structural diagrams). Exclude sequential flowcharts (*Flow Diagrams*) and quantitative data plots (*Graphs*). Include text-drawn diagrams made from ASCII or Unicode characters, including fenced code or preformatted blocks. An image attachment is not required. Inspect preserved line breaks, spacing, endpoints, and connectors. Exclude ordinary prose, lists, executable code, and isolated chemical formulas without a schematic spatial representation. Apply the same structural criteria in every language and translation; translating labels alone does not add or remove a diagram.

count.description: Occurrences within this section. Tag multi-line visual representations of sequential processes, algorithms, decision trees, state machines, or workflows with directional arrows. Require more than one meaningful visual row or level. A single-line sequence such as "Input → Process → Output" is not a Flow Diagram, even when bold, fenced as code, or automatically wrapped onto several screen lines. Prose, numbered instructions, and line breaks alone do not qualify. For images, SVG, or Mermaid, judge the rendered visual layout, not serialized source line counts. A top-to-bottom multi-level process or a branching decision diagram qualifies when connected stages span multiple visual rows or levels. Exclude static structural diagrams without sequential flow (Diagrams & Illustrations). Count each complete qualifying diagram once, not its rows, stages, or arrows.

count.description: Occurrences within this section. Tag formal symbolic math, equations, formulas, or variables rendered via LaTeX or mathematical symbols (e.g., standalone equations, inline variables like $x$ or $\theta$, chemical reaction equations). Exclude plain-text numbers, dates, currency, or percentages. Chemical formulas and species names alone do not qualify, even with subscripts, superscripts, ionic charges, or LaTeX formatting (e.g., H2O, CO2, NaCl, or Ca2+). Count chemical notation only when it represents a reaction with reactants and products; a list or comparison of chemical formulas is not a reaction. An actual mathematical calculation involving chemical quantities can still qualify as math; do not count its chemical species separately. Count one cohesive notation sequence or connected derivation once within its section, including its general formula, substitutions, rearrangements, intermediate steps, and final answer. Count unrelated notation sequences separately; do not count each variable or line within the same sequence. Standalone formal symbolic variables qualify when outside an already counted sequence. Symbolic comparisons and ordered relationships qualify whether the compared terms are variables, numerical values, or descriptive labels. Exclude isolated plain-text numbers, dates, currency, percentages, and unit labels. Centering, bold text, or TeX formatting alone does not establish Mathematical Notation.

count.description: Occurrences within this section. Tag an ordered explanation containing at least two distinct, linked procedural steps that demonstrate how to execute a procedure, derive a formula, or solve a problem. Each step must advance the same procedure toward its outcome. A single-step explanation, one substitution, one arithmetic operation, or an answer with a brief explanation is not a Step-by-Step Walkthrough, even when numbered or spread across several lines. Unordered facts and independent one-step examples do not become a walkthrough merely by appearing together. Count each cohesive procedure or worked solution once, not each step. When the same walkthrough continues across consecutive sections, treat that uninterrupted sequence as one walkthrough and assign its count only to the section where the walkthrough starts. Later consecutive sections that continue that procedure receive no additional walkthrough count. The sequence as a whole must contain at least two linked steps; those steps may span consecutive sections. Do not combine unrelated single-step explanations. This is continuation counting, not conversation-wide deduplication: a walkthrough independently presented again later can count as a new occurrence, even if it uses the same method or problem. Sharing a topic or similar wording alone does not establish continuation. Keep the count on its starting section and preserve all persistent section IDs; do not merge or renumber sections. A specific worked example can receive both Examples and Step-by-Step Walkthroughs when it meets this multi-step requirement. A general procedure without a concrete instance is a Walkthrough only. Do not additionally count the procedural steps as Lists / Bullet Points.

Count separately presented cases separately. A case independently presented again in another section receives a count in that section. count.description: Occurrences within this section. Tag utterances whose conversational function is directly engaging the learner socially: acknowledging or registering their input, validating feelings or confusion, expressing empathy, praising effort or contributions, encouraging them, friendly greetings or pleasantries, or establishing collaboration and rapport. Short expressions such as "Okay", "Got it", and "Great question!" qualify when context establishes this social function; no minimum word count or substantive-engagement threshold applies. Apply the same contextual criteria in English, Tamil, and other languages. An acknowledgment such as "Yes" or "No" can qualify, but a bare domain answer or quoted example does not automatically qualify. Count one cohesive conversational move once within its section, even when expressed across multiple sentences. Count separately expressed social moves separately, such as a distinct acknowledgment followed by distinct encouragement; do not count each word or sentence of one cohesive move separately. Highlight the complete conversational expression, excluding adjacent factual explanation. This overrides the general two-to-eight-word highlight preference for Social Cues. Keep each exact-source highlight within its owning section and the existing 500-character limit; for an exceptionally long expression, use the shortest complete utterance establishing the social move. Exclude factual explanations, neutral organizational transitions, quoted examples, and instructional wording without a social function. "Let's work through this together" establishes collaboration and qualifies; "Next, consider atomic size" and purely procedural "Let's calculate the radius" do not qualify alone. Domain-knowledge questions belong to Questions, self-report pulse-checks to Comprehension Checks, and follow-up offers to Next Step Suggestions; these do not become Social Cues merely through friendly wording. Add Social Cues alongside these labels only for a separately identifiable social expression.

count.description: Occurrences within this section. Tag any span where the chatbot makes a mistake. This includes factual inaccuracies, hallucinated facts or citations, mathematical or logical calculation errors, internal self-contradictions, broken formatting or rendering glitches (e.g., unrendered LaTeX or broken tables), or pedagogical failures (e.g., directly giving away the final answer when the user explicitly asked for just a hint). Can be double-tagged over any structural or pedagogical element that contains the error. Count each distinct confirmed error once within its section, including its supporting explanation; repeated references to the same error within that occurrence do not add counts. Require evidence that the bot asserts the error or that the supplied rendering actually fails. Corrected learner errors, deliberately marked incorrect examples, valid source markup, unfamiliar terminology, language differences, and ordinary stylistic preferences alone are not bot errors. Do not infer a rendering failure from valid Markdown or LaTeX source alone. Treat uncertain or unverifiable claims as uncertain rather than confirmed errors. Judge the supplied conversation version; do not attribute an unseen source-language error to its translation or vice versa.

Corrected learner errors, deliberately marked incorrect examples, valid source markup, unfamiliar terminology, language differences, and ordinary stylistic preferences alone are not bot errors. Do not infer a rendering failure from valid Markdown or LaTeX source alone. Treat uncertain or unverifiable claims as uncertain rather than confirmed errors. Judge the supplied conversation version; do not attribute an unseen source-language error to its translation or vice versa.

instructional_features.description: Captured interaction states are supporting views of the original containing section, not additional sections or additional components. A quiz with three questions remains three questions when the learner selects an answer, views feedback, or navigates Previous/Next. Count each question/image in that component once across its supporting views. Separate components in the same section remain separate; do not deduplicate merely by matching text. Supporting-view captions and capture metadata do not count as headings.

llm_evidence.description: Optional single-line model justification. HTML capture labels reference their owning section ID and do not require transcript spans.

section_highlights.description: Optional short exact-source anchors, one per counted text occurrence; occurrence is scoped to the owning section.
